She mentions some controversy regarding an author named Philip Roth and the inspiration of a character in his book "The Human Stain."

There was an interesting look at a different perspective in an article I found here: http://archive.is/e6wit

This "wikistrategies" article declares Sharyl Attkinson's presentation as a "misleading characterization" of Roth's disagreement with wikipedia.

In private correspondence with a Wikipedia editor – noted here, in an unprecedented violation of Wikipedia policy, and in a way that no reader can verify independently — Roth further elaborated that the character was in fact based on his friend Melvin Tumin.[citation needed]

This is the example "wikistrategies" gives as a reason why there needs to be a published fact to cite in order to substantiate the claims of wikipedia.

However, in the now updated wikipedia and infogalactic page, there is a 2008 interview cited in which Philip Roth clearly explains he was not aware of Anatole Broyard when he created his own literary character that was similar. There was already a public, citable "fact." So why did wikipedia hold out until Roth wrote an open letter to wikipedia four years later?

His gripe was not about whether or not he was a "credible, citable" source, the gripe was that the original allegation of Anatole Broyard as the inspiration for his character was completely unsubstantiated by guesses from literary critics.

It's fine that anyone takes away what they want from literature. One could certainly draw many parallels between Broyard and the character, but wikipedia was trying to make a claim about the actual thought process that Roth was using to create literature based on literary critics' assumptions. All they had to do was include a disclaimer that this was not the opinion of the author himself. Then they try to defend it with convoluted bullshit about their retarded process of "wikistrategies."

But in this instance, Wikipedia’s editors nailed it. They held the line against the wishes of a popular author, who had requested special treatment, and whose request was wholly without merit.

This subtle jab at Sharyl Attkinson in this "wikistrategies" article comes across as if it's astroturfing within astroturfing, or nested astroturfing if you will.

TL;DR: Fuck Wikipedia. Use infogalactic instead.
